g.text: F4. In panel (a), D2 s44 is the ONE unresolvable pair - the between-arm gap is 1.4 sampling standard deviations - and section 4.6's D2 "2 of 3" depends on it. It is not a hit; it

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: is a pair the metric cannot separate, which is why T1 marks that cell unresolvable in every row. Panel (c) constrains the TYPICAL spread and essentially not the tail: three

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: repetitions cannot rule out the liveness gate's 25% divergence rate (P(0 in 3 | p = 0.25) = 0.42; the exact upper 95% bound from 0 of 3 is p <= 0.63), and the design was cut from

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: ten repetitions to three because a ten-way launch exhausted GPU memory. Panel (c)'s statistic is R3 on a training probe and must not share an axis with (a)'s and (d)'s R1 on

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: held-out artifacts; they are drawn on separate axes for that reason. Panel (a) and F3 are not in conflict: (a) holds the model fixed and varies the patient sample, F3 holds the

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: step fixed and varies the seed. Panel (b) shares its data with F1(a). The faithful RankMe of panel (d) is computed on OUR OWN artifacts and is an internal comparison; no number

text.style: font-size: 6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #5a5a5a

g.text: in this paper is plotted against a published RankMe value, because RankMe's epsilon sits outside the division and its p_k do not sum to 1.
